skill.name: axe-ios-simulator
skill.description: Guide for using AXe CLI to automate iOS Simulator gestures, text input, screenshots, video capture, and accessibility inspection.
skill.summary: Automate iOS Simulator interactions and accessibility checks with AXe CLI workflows.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline command formatting, and documented AXe simulator actions. Confirmed low-risk findings involve local screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection that can expose app UI data; one medium semantic issue covers third-party Homebrew installation.

remediation.suggestion: Ask users to verify the Homebrew tap and AXe release before installation, and document the required trust boundary.
Add a warning to use test data and review screenshots, videos, streams, and accessibility dumps before sharing.
State that commands should run only against a confirmed simulator UDID and only after user approval.

content.user_title: Automate iOS Simulator Testing with AXe
content.value_statement: Manual simulator testing slows mobile development and accessibility review. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise AXe CLI workflows for gestures, screenshots, video, and UI inspection.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation of the AXe CLI with Homebrew.
Shows how to list simulators and scope commands with a simulator UDID.
Provides tap, swipe, gesture, touch, button, text, and key input examples.
Explains screenshot capture, video recording, and MJPEG or ffmpeg streaming commands.
Shows accessibility tree inspection for a full screen or a point.
Includes automation patterns for waiting, scrolling, forms, and post-action screenshots.
limitations: Requires macOS, Xcode Simulator, and the AXe CLI installed locally.
Does not create or manage iOS Simulator devices by itself.
Commands can only act on simulators reachable from the current machine.
Screenshots, video, and accessibility output may include sensitive app data.

use_cases.title: Repeat Mobile UI Flows
use_cases.description: Exercise common simulator flows with repeatable CLI actions during feature work.

use_cases.title: Capture Test Evidence
use_cases.description: Create screenshots or short recordings that document simulator behavior during manual checks.

use_cases.title: Inspect Accessibility State
use_cases.description: Read the simulator accessibility tree to verify labels, traits, and reachable controls.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Simulators
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the axe-ios-simulator skill to list available iOS Simulators and tell me which UDID to use.

prompt_templates.title: Tap and Type in a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to tap the Email field, type a test email, submit the form, and capture the result.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to describe the current simulator UI, identify the Submit button, and suggest the safest tap action.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a Scroll Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to scan the UI, scroll until targetElement appears, tap it, record a short video, and summarize each step.

output_examples.input: Find the simulator, tap the Submit button, and capture the result.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the target simulator, confirms the Submit control, performs the tap, waits, and reports the screenshot path.

output_examples.input: Record a quick demo of a login flow.
output_examples.output: The response performs the requested simulator actions, records the flow, stops recording, and reports the saved video path.

output_examples.input: Check accessibility information around a screen point.
output_examples.output: The response inspects the requested location, summarizes accessible labels and traits, and recommends the next interaction.

best_practices: Confirm the target simulator UDID before running commands.
Use test accounts and non-sensitive fixture data for typed input.
Review generated screenshots, videos, and UI dumps before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Running commands against an unknown simulator.
Typing real passwords or customer data into test flows.
Treating generated media or accessibility output as safe to publish by default.

faq.question: What platform does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires macOS with Xcode Simulator and the AXe CLI available locally.

faq.question: Does this skill install AXe automatically?
faq.answer: It provides Homebrew installation guidance. The user or environment must allow that installation.

faq.question: Can it control physical iPhones?
faq.answer: The source documents iOS Simulator automation. It does not document physical device control.

faq.question: Can it inspect accessibility labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to describe the full UI tree or inspect a specific screen point.

faq.question: Does it send captured data to external services?
faq.answer: The source does not instruct uploads. Installation through Homebrew may access package repositories.

faq.question: How should screenshots and videos be handled?
faq.answer: Treat them as sensitive project artifacts and share them only under the project policy.
